settings.copy: Field & Frame is an architecture studio designing civic buildings, workplaces, and homes that balance light, material, and the life that moves through them — from first sketch to final key.

trust_list.text: Full service: concept through construction administration
30 years of civic, workplace, and residential work
Licensed in six states and growing

settings.title: Design that
settings.intro: We don't chase trends. We design for how a building is actually used — the morning light in a classroom, the sound in a lobby, the way a corridor guides two people toward a conversation.

features.title: Site-first thinking
features.text: We read the land before we draw on it — sun angles, prevailing wind, the neighbor's roofline, the history of the street. The site is the first client.
features.detail: Every scheme begins with a site study

features.title: Material honesty
features.text: Brick, timber, stone, and steel used for what they are. We avoid cladding that pretends to be structure and choose materials that age gracefully rather than peel.
features.detail: Materials chosen to age, not expire

features.title: Light as a structural material
features.text: A room is a machine for shaping daylight. We place openings to bring the low winter sun deep inside and cut glare before it becomes a problem.

features.title: Carbon-conscious by default
features.text: We model embodied carbon on every project and favor reuse, low-carbon concrete, and timber where it's honest. Sustainability isn't a badge here — it's the default.

features.title: Built for real budgets
features.text: We cost our designs with real contractors, not guesswork. The building you approve in the render is the building that shows up on site — and on budget.

features.title: We stay through construction
features.text: Our architects run construction administration ourselves. When a detail meets a difficult condition on site, we're there to resolve it, not to hand it off.

settings.title: From blank site to
settings.intro: A disciplined, honest path from first conversation to completed structure.

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: We start with your program and your land — how you live or work, what the site gives you, and what you've learned from buildings that fell short.

steps.title: Study
steps.text: We test the site with sun, wind, and circulation studies, and sketch three directions before we ever settle on one worth drawing well.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: The chosen scheme becomes a full set of drawings and a real model — plans, sections, and a budget you can actually hold us to.

steps.title: Refine
steps.text: You live with the design through a few honest rounds. We refine materials, daylight, and cost together until it's right, not just finished.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: We produce construction documents, help you choose a contractor, and run construction administration to keep the intent intact through the last nail.

settings.note: Most of our work arrives as a referral from a client who says the same thing: the building felt right the day they moved in — and still does years later.

reviews.quote: They found budget headroom we didn't think existed and poured it into daylight. Our librarians say the reading room gets busier every year, and I believe it's the room itself doing the work.

reviews.quote: Field & Frame costed our renovation honestly from the first meeting. Nothing came as a surprise at the end, and the building is everything the model promised — that almost never happens.

reviews.quote: We've built three homes with them. The first one taught us what 'light' could mean; by the third we stopped asking for anything and just described how we wanted to live.
